statement: Ammonia inhibition review: acetoclastic methanogens are the most ammonia-sensitive group, hydrogenotrophic methanogens the most tolerant, with Methanosarcina intermediate.
Syntrophic acetate oxidation coupled to hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis can replace acetoclastic methanogenesis when ammonia rises.
Syntrophic acetate-oxidising consortia enriched from full-scale mesophilic digesters are taxonomically diverse, with unclassified Clostridia and Syntrophomonas recurring.
Low- vs high-ammonia full-scale digesters differ in bacterial composition and fhs profiles, with novel candidate syntrophic acetate oxidisers among uncultured Clostridia.
Ammonia dosing of digester sludge inhibited syntrophic propionate oxidation, with Smithella, Methanosaetaceae and Methanospirillaceae among the inhibited populations.
Several of the most abundant populations in full-scale digesters are inactive immigrants from the feed; inactive populations were associated with aerobes and facultative anaerobes.
